title: Ordinary sections-tensor square for restriction by a point automorphism
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $g:s\to s$ be any scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For each finite coefficient field $F\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, let $\mathcal O_F$ be its valuation ring with a chosen uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], put $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and write $G_F=g^{-1}$ with the $R_F$-action transported through $c_F^{-1}$ [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Sections $\Gamma(s,-)$ are termwise sections passed to derived categories [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

Let $E\subset L$ be two such fields. For $H\in D(R_E)$, the unbounded derived category of sheaves of $R_E$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], put $C_{L/E}H=H\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L$. Let $b_H:C_{L/E}G_EH\xrightarrow{\sim}G_LC_{L/E}H$ be the canonical inverse-image tensor comparison, with its flat-term K-flat representative specified by [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model]. Let $\theta_H:\Gamma(s,H)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\to\Gamma(s,C_{L/E}H)$ be exactly the ordinary derived sections-tensor map of [lem-weil-point-derived-sections-tensor-descent], and let $\sigma^{g,F}$ be the restriction/coprojection map of [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural]. Then
$$\Gamma(s,b_H)\theta_{G_EH}(\sigma^{g,E}_H\otimes1)=\sigma^{g,L}_{C_{L/E}H}\theta_H.$$
This holds without boundedness, constructibility or derived-completeness assumptions on $H$.

On every flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to H$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the two composites are represented by equal chain maps. Write $U=(s,\mathrm{id})$ and $V=(s,g)$. Under the evaluation identification $(G_FM)(U)\cong M(V)$ of [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural], applied in the common target to $F=L$ and $M=C_{L/E}P=P\otimes_{R_E}R_L$, so that $\Gamma(s,G_LC_{L/E}P^n)\cong(P^n\otimes_{R_E}R_L)(V)$, their common degreewise value on $x\otimes a$, with $x\in P^n(U)$ and $a\in\mathcal O_L$, is the sheafification image of $x|_V\otimes a_s|_V$, where $a_s$ is the constant-value section of [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor]. The coefficient value is normalized by $\sigma^{g,L}_{R_L}(a_s)=c_L^{-1}(a_s)$. These chain maps represent the displayed derived equality independently of the chosen resolution, using sheafified tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; no assertion that arbitrary sheaf tensor sections are sectionwise tensors is made.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to H$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model], $G_EP$ is flat-term K-flat, $Q=P\otimes_{R_E}R_L$ represents $C_{L/E}H$, and $b_P:G_EP\otimes_{R_E}R_L\to G_LQ$ represents exactly $b_H$. By [lem-weil-point-derived-sections-tensor-descent], the two occurrences of $\theta$ are represented by their termwise balanced maps on $P$ and $G_EP$. By [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural], the occurrences of $\sigma$ are termwise restriction/coprojection maps. Thus both sides can be calculated as maps from $\Gamma(s,P)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ to $\Gamma(s,G_LQ)$.

proof.text: Fix $n$, $x\in P^n(U)$, and $a\in\mathcal O_L$, with constant-value section $a_s$ as in [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor]. Put $y=\sigma^{g,E}_{P^n}(x)$. By [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural], $y$ identifies with $x|_V$ and $\sigma^{g,L}_{R_L}(a_s)=c_L^{-1}(a_s)$ identifies with $a_s|_V$. The left composite first sends $x\otimes a$ to the sheafification image of $y\otimes a_s$. In the local formula for $b_P$ in [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model], the second input $a_s$ is $c_L(c_L^{-1}(a_s))$. Consequently its output, in the evaluation target $Q^n(V)$, is precisely the sheafification image of $x|_V\otimes a_s|_V$. This substitution also checks the transported coefficient action; it does not replace that action by an untwisted one.

proof.text: For the right composite, [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor] sends $x\otimes a$ to the sheafification image of $x\otimes a_s$ over $U$. By [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural] its subsequent $\sigma^{g,L}_{Q^n}$ is restriction to $V$ under evaluation. The presheaf tensor restriction in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] sends $x\otimes a_s$ to $x|_V\otimes a_s|_V$; the map to its sheafification is a morphism of presheaves by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], hence commutes with this restriction. This gives exactly the value in Step 2. Pure tensors generate the algebraic tensor module in the source, so the two linear maps agree in every degree. Only the source is generated this way: no surjectivity of the presheaf-to-sheaf tensor map on arbitrary sections is used.

proof.text: The maps $\theta$, $\sigma$ and $b_P$ are chain maps by [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor, lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural, lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model]; tensoring with the degree-zero coefficient module adds no differential or sign. Steps 2-3 therefore give equality of chain maps. Apply localization to this equality. Sections preserve quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. The specified $\theta$ maps and their resolution identifications are independent of $P$ by [lem-weil-point-derived-sections-tensor-descent]; the same holds for $b$ by [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model], and derived naturality of $\sigma$ is in [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural]. Conjugating the localized equality by these identifications gives the displayed equality for $H$. Repeating it for any other resolution gives that same equality, because each identification is the specified one. All cited assertions apply to unbounded ambient complexes, so no constructibility or completeness is needed.
